rows.fact: The Bihar SIR order made an additional Declaration Form (Annexure D) compulsory for anyone applying in Form 6 as a new elector, or in Form 8 when shifting into Bihar from another state.
rows.quote: Further, in case of application for registration as a new elector or for shifting from outside the state of Bihar, it is also directed that henceforth, alongwith Form 6/Form 8, an additional Declaration Form (Annexure D) shall also be required to be filled by the applicant to support the declaration made therein.
rows.page_or_para: Order No.23/ERS/2025 dated 24.06.2025, para 15, order page 6 of 19 (PDF page 9) (ECI document, copy hosted by CEO Kerala as Annexure I to ECI letter No.23/2025-ERS (Vol.II) of 27.10.2025)

rows.fact: In Annexure D the applicant declared being over 18, ordinarily resident and a citizen, and ticked one birth cohort. Born in India before 01.07.1987 meant a document for self. Born between 01.07.1987 and 02.12.2004 meant a document for self and one for father or mother. Born after 02.12.2004 meant documents for self, father and mother, plus a parent's passport and visa if a parent was not Indian.
rows.quote: (i) I am above 18 years of age, ordinary resident on the above address, and citizen of India, and (tick any one) [ ] I was born in India before 01.07.1987 • Provide any document, for Self, from the list given below establishing date of birth and/or place of birth. [ ] I was born in India between 01.07.1987 and 02.12.2004 • Provide any document, for Self, from the list given below establishing date of birth and/or place of birth. • Provide any document, for Father or Mother, from the list given below establishing date of birth and/or place of birth. [ ] I was born in India after 02.12.2004 • Provide any document, for Self, from the list given below establishing date of birth and/or place of birth. • Provide any document, for Father, from the list given below establishing date of birth and/or place of birth. • Provide any document, for Mother, from the list given below establishing date of birth and/or place of birth. • If any parent is not Indian, provide a copy of his/her valid passport & visa at the time of your birth.
rows.page_or_para: Annexure D (Declaration Form), order page 18 of 19 (PDF page 21) (ECI document, copy hosted by CEO Kerala as Annexure I to ECI letter No.23/2025-ERS (Vol.II) of 27.10.2025)

rows.fact: Annexure D also covered people born outside India and those who became citizens by registration or naturalisation, and required the applicant to declare no other citizenship and no other enrolment, under penalty of Section 31 of the RP Act 1950.
rows.quote: [ ] I was born outside of India (attach proof of Birth Registration issued by Indian Mission abroad), [ ] I have acquired Indian citizenship by Registration/Naturalisation (attach Certificate of Registration of Citizenship) (ii) I have not acquired the citizenship of any other country. (iii) I am applying for inclusion in the Electoral Roll and my name is not included in any other Assembly Constituency/ Parliamentary Constituency. (iv) I am aware that making the above statement or declaration in relation to this application which is false ... is punishable under Section 31 of Representation of the People Act,1950
rows.page_or_para: Annexure D, order page 18 of 19 (PDF page 21) (ECI document, copy hosted by CEO Kerala as Annexure I to ECI letter No.23/2025-ERS (Vol.II) of 27.10.2025)

rows.fact: The documents behind Annexure D were an indicative list of 11, self-attested separately for self, father and mother. An extract of the Bihar roll with qualifying date 01.01.2003 counted as sufficient on its own.
rows.quote: Indicative (not exhaustive) list of documents to be submitted in support of the declaration (separate self attested documents to be submitted for Self, Father and Mother, if mentioned above, except where extract of the Electoral Roll of Bihar with qualifying date 01.01.2003 is used, which will be considered as a sufficient document in itself)
rows.page_or_para: Annexure D, order page 19 of 19 (PDF page 22) (ECI document, copy hosted by CEO Kerala as Annexure I to ECI letter No.23/2025-ERS (Vol.II) of 27.10.2025)

rows.fact: Every Form 6 claim had to carry the new Declaration Form, including Form 6 applications already pending and advance claims for 01.10.2025. Form 8 needed it only for shifting from outside Bihar.
rows.quote: Every claim for inclusion of name in the roll as new elector shall be in Form-6 along with new Declaration Form. Henceforth, all EROs shall also ensure to collect the prescribed Declaration Form in respect of all pending Form 6 and advance claims received in Form 6 w.r.t. 01.10.2025 as the qualifying date. ... New Declaration Form shall be submitted alongwith Form-8 for shifting of residence from outside the state of Bihar.
rows.page_or_para: Annexure B (Guidelines) paras 5(d) and 5(e), order page 11 of 19 (PDF page 14) (ECI document, copy hosted by CEO Kerala as Annexure I to ECI letter No.23/2025-ERS (Vol.II) of 27.10.2025)

rows.fact: An existing elector who missed the enumeration deadline could get back on the roll only by filing Form 6 with Annexure D during the claims and objections period.
rows.quote: In case any elector is unable to submit their filled in enumeration forms within the specified time, they may file Form 6 alongwith the prescribed Declaration Form (Annexure D) for inclusion during the claims and objections period.
rows.page_or_para: Annexure B (Guidelines) para 4(c), order page 10 of 19 (PDF page 13) (ECI document, copy hosted by CEO Kerala as Annexure I to ECI letter No.23/2025-ERS (Vol.II) of 27.10.2025)

rows.state: India (Phase II: A&NI, Chhattisgarh, Goa, Gujarat, Kerala, Lakshadweep, Madhya Pradesh, Puducherry, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal)
rows.fact: For Phase II the Commission replaced Annexure D with a modified Declaration Form (Annexure IV). It asks for the applicant's or a relative's entry in the last SIR roll and three declarations, and has no birth-cohort tick boxes on the form itself.
rows.quote: Declaration Form (To be submitted along with Form 6/Form 8 for enrolment as a new Elector/shifting from outside the state) ... Details of the Elector in the Electoral Roll of the last SIR (if applicable) | Details of the Relative, whose name is given in the previous column, in the last SIR ... (i) I have not acquired the citizenship of any other country. (ii) I am applying for inclusion in the Electoral Roll through Form 6, and my name is not included in any other Assembly Constituency/Parliamentary Constituency. Or I am applying for inclusion in the Electoral Roll through Form 8 on shifting. (iii) I am aware that making the above statement or declaration ... is punishable under Section 31 of Representation of the People Act,1950
rows.page_or_para: ECI letter No.23/2025-ERS (Vol.II) dated 27.10.2025, para 2(c) and Annexure IV (PDF page 27) (ECI letter, copy hosted by CEO Kerala)

rows.fact: Under Annexure IV documents are asked for only after a notice, when the last-SIR details given are unavailable or do not match the database. The same three birth cohorts then decide whose documents are needed.
rows.quote: ERO will issue notices to those applicants whose previous SIR Electoral Roll(s) details provided in the Declaration Form are either unavailable or do not match the database. Upon receipt of notice, the applicant to provide the documents based upon the following categories: If born in India before 01.07.1987 ... If born in India between 01.07.1987 and 02.12.2004 ... Provide any document, for Father or Mother ... If born in India after 02.12.2004 ... Provide any document, for Father ... Provide any document, for Mother ... If any parent is not Indian, provide a copy of his/her valid passport & visa at the time of your birth.
rows.page_or_para: Information Sheet for Declaration Form (PDF page 28) (ECI letter of 27.10.2025, copy hosted by CEO Kerala)

rows.fact: The Phase II document list keeps the 11 documents and adds Aadhaar under the 09.09.2025 letter as item 12 and an extract of the Bihar SIR roll of 01.07.2025 as item 13.
rows.quote: 12. For Aadhaar, the Commission's directions issued vide letter No. 23/2025-ERS/Vol.II dated 09.09.2025 (Annexure II) shall apply. 13. Extract of the electoral roll of Bihar SIR with reference to 01.07.2025.
rows.page_or_para: Information Sheet for Declaration Form, items 12 and 13 (PDF page 28)

rows.fact: The Phase III letter applies the same modified Declaration Form (Annexure IV) with Form 6 and with Form 8 for shifting from outside the state. Its operative declarations are worded as in Phase II.
rows.quote: c. Modified Enumeration Form (Annexure III) and Declaration Form (Annexure IV) shall be applicable for SIR in these States/UTs. ... Annexure-IV Declaration Form (To be submitted along with Form 6/Form 8 for enrolment as a new Elector/shifting from outside the state) ... (i) I have not acquired the citizenship of any other country. (ii) I am applying for inclusion in the Electoral Roll through Form 6, and my name is not included in any other Assembly Constituency/Parliamentary Constituency. Or I am applying for inclusion in the Electoral Roll through Form 8 on shifting.
rows.page_or_para: ECI letter No.23/2025-ERS (Vol.II) dated 14.05.2026, para 2(c) (PDF page 2) and Annexure IV (PDF page 27) (ECI document, copy hosted by CEO Maharashtra)

rows.fact: The Phase III document list has 12 items. The Bihar SIR roll extract (item 13 in Phase II) is not in it, and item 10 reads Family Register maintained by government officials under any statutory or administrative regulation, where Phase II said prepared by State or local authorities.
rows.quote: 10.Family Register maintained by Govt. officials under any Statute/Administrative Regulation 11.Any land/house allotment certificate by the Government 12.For Aadhaar, the Commission's directions issued vide letter No. 23/2025-ERS/Vol.II dated 09.09.2025 (Annexure II) shall apply. ***
rows.page_or_para: Information Sheet for Declaration Form (PDF page 28); compare CEO Kerala copy of the Phase II sheet, PDF page 28

rows.fact: In Phase III a person may link to their own or a relative's entry in the last intensive revision of the state concerned. For states already revised, Annexure V lists both the old revision and the SIR qualifying date, so the Bihar SIR roll of 01.07.2025 and the Phase II rolls of 01.01.2026 count as last-revision rolls.
rows.quote: e. Any person can link himself/herself with his/her or relative's entries in electoral rolls of the relevant last intensive revisions of the respective States/UTs, as mentioned in Annexure V. ... B- Last SIR qualifying date for Other States/UTs ... 3 Bihar 01.01.2003 & 01.07.2025 ... 17 West Bengal 01.01.2002 & 01.01.2026
rows.page_or_para: Para 2(e) (PDF page 2) and Annexure V Table B (PDF page 29) (ECI document, copy hosted by CEO Maharashtra)

rows.fact: Booth Level Agents of recognised parties were allowed to file applications in bulk, up to 50 forms a day to the BLO before the draft roll and 10 a day after it, with a list and an undertaking that they had personally verified each one.
rows.quote: With a view to ensure more involvement of political parties, the Commission has allowed BLAs of recognized political parties to file applications in bulk, subject to the condition that a BLA shall not submit more than 50 Forms/day to BLO before the Draft Publication, and 10 Forms/day thereafter. BLA will submit a list of application forms with an undertaking that he has personally verified the particulars of the application forms and is satisfied that they are correct.
rows.page_or_para: Annexure B (Guidelines) para 9(d)(iii)-(iv), order page 13 of 19 (PDF page 16) (ECI document, copy hosted by CEO Kerala as Annexure I to ECI letter No.23/2025-ERS (Vol.II) of 27.10.2025)

rows.fact: The Commission told parties that electors who missed the enumeration deadline could apply in Form 6 with a declaration during claims and objections, and that BLAs could keep submitting up to 10 forms a day after the draft.
rows.quote: Electors who miss the initial deadline can still apply during the claims and objections period using Form 6 along with a declaration form. BLAs can continue to submit up to 10 forms per day even after the Draft Roll is published.
rows.page_or_para: ECI Press Note No. ECI/PN/240/2025 dated 03.07.2025, compilation PDF page 46 (compilation hosted by CEO Bihar)

rows.fact: At the final roll the Commission said anyone eligible could still apply for inclusion up to ten days before the last date for nominations.
rows.quote: If any eligible person still wishes to apply for inclusion of their name in Electoral Roll, they can submit an application up to ten days before last date for filing nominations for election.
rows.page_or_para: PIB release ID 2173316 (30 Sep 2025), point 6

rows.fact: BLOs were told to carry at least 30 blank Form 6 with blank Annexure IV declarations during house to house enumeration, and EROs to invite advance applications for 1 April, 1 July and 1 October 2026.
rows.quote: g. During House to House Enumeration, BLO to carry at least 30 blank Form 6 along with blank Declaration Forms (Annexure IV), to supply to anyone who seeks to enrol as a new elector. h. ERO shall also invite advance applications for subsequent qualifying dates i.e. 1st April, 1st July & 1st October, 2026 while publishing notice for draft publication in Form-5.
rows.page_or_para: ECI letter dated 27.10.2025, paras 2(g) and 2(h), letter page 2 of 3

rows.fact: The Phase III letter repeats the 30 blank Form 6 with declarations for BLOs and asks EROs to invite advance applications for the later qualifying dates of the year. It also annexes the 24.06.2025 order and guidelines unchanged, including the BLA limit of 50 forms a day before the draft and 10 after.
rows.quote: g. During House to House Enumeration, BLO to carry at least 30 blank Form 6 along with blank Declaration Forms (Annexure IV), to supply to anyone who seeks to enrol as a new elector. h. ERO shall also invite advance applications for subsequent qualifying dates of the year while publishing notice for draft publication in Form-5.
rows.page_or_para: ECI letter dated 14.05.2026, paras 2(g) and 2(h) (PDF page 2); guidelines para 9(d)(iii) at PDF page 16 (ECI document, copy hosted by CEO Maharashtra)

rows.fact: Announcing Phase III enumeration, the Commission said electors who missed the 28.06.2026 enumeration deadline may apply through Form 6 with the prescribed Declaration Form, and that BLAs may collect up to 50 forms a day before the draft.
rows.quote: Electors who are unable to submit their Enumeration Forms by 28.06.2026 may apply through Form 6 along with the prescribed Declaration Form during the claims and objections period. ... the Commission has allowed Booth Level Agents (BLAs) of recognized political parties to collect from the public, up to 50 Forms/day and hand it over to the BLO before the Draft Publication.
rows.page_or_para: PIB release ID 2267217 (31 May 2026)

rows.fact: The CEO told parties that EROs would collect the prescribed Declaration Form for all pending Form 6 applications and advance claims for the qualifying date of 1 October 2026.
rows.quote: EROs have also been instructed to collect the prescribed Declaration Form in respect of all pending Form 6 applications and advance claims received with reference to the qualifying date of 1st October, 2026.
rows.page_or_para: PIB Shillong release ID 2294476 (04 Aug 2026)

rows.fact: After its meeting of 26.09.2026 the Commission said the SIR declaration stays with Form 6 during SIR and that outside the SIR period the forms of the Registration of Electors Rules 1960 will be used.
rows.quote: The declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR has been upheld by the Hon'ble Supreme Court. For non-SIR period, the Forms applicable as per Rules (the Registration of Electors Rules 1960) will be used.
rows.page_or_para: PIB release ID 2315309 (26 Sep 2026), third decision

rows.fact: The Form 6 PDF served on the Voters' Service Portal on 2 October 2026 is the Rules form. It cites Rules 13(1) and 26, lists date-of-birth and residence documents, and carries a five-part declaration with no birth cohorts and no parents' documents.
rows.quote: (See Rules 13(1) and (26) of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960) ... DECLARATION I HEREBY DECLARE that to the best of my knowledge and belief- (i) I am a citizen of India and place of my birth is:- Village/Town ... (ii) I am ordinarily a resident at the address mentioned at Sr. No. 8(a) in Form 6 since ... (iii) I am applying for inclusion in Electoral Roll for the first time and my name is not included in any Assembly Constituency/ Parliamentary Constituency.
rows.page_or_para: Form 6, pages 1-2 (file metadata dated 28.10.2025); this is the downloadable form, not the online form flow

rows.fact: The Bihar order barred EROs from deleting any entry from the draft roll without an inquiry and a fair and reasonable opportunity to the person concerned, with appeals to the District Magistrate and then the CEO.
rows.quote: The ERO/AERO shall not delete any entry from the draft roll without conducting an inquiry and giving a fair and reasonable opportunity to the persons concerned whose name has appeared in the draft roll.
rows.page_or_para: Order dated 24.06.2025, para 14, order page 6 of 19 (PDF page 9) (ECI document, copy hosted by CEO Kerala as Annexure I to ECI letter No.23/2025-ERS (Vol.II) of 27.10.2025)

rows.fact: EROs had to list claims and objections in Forms 9, 10, 11, 11A and 11B, show them on a notice board daily, put them on the CEO website so citizens could object to any claim, and give them to parties weekly. CEOs were to post all Forms 6, 6A, 7 and 8 received on their website daily.
rows.quote: ERO shall prepare lists of claims and objections in Form 9, 10, 11 and 11A and 11B and exhibit one copy of such lists on a notice board in his office on every working day. ... The list of all claims and objections received should also be put up on the website of the CEO so that citizens are able to see the list and lodge objections, if any, with the concerned ERO. ... Computerization and posting of all application forms received in Forms 6, 6A, 7, 8 on the website of the CEO on a day to day basis.
rows.page_or_para: Annexure B (Guidelines) paras 6(a)-(d) (PDF page 14) and 9(a)(v) (PDF page 15) (ECI document, copy hosted by CEO Kerala as Annexure I to ECI letter No.23/2025-ERS (Vol.II) of 27.10.2025)

rows.fact: Form 7 objections and Form 8 corrections received after an election is announced are to be decided only after the election, because deletions are barred from the tenth day of the election programme.
rows.quote: There is a complete restriction on deletion of names & corrections in particulars of electors after 10th day of the announcement of election programme, therefore all Form-7 and Form-8 (other than shifting) received after the announcement of election shall be disposed of after the election is over.
rows.page_or_para: Annexure B (Guidelines) para 12(b), order page 15 of 19 (PDF page 18 of the Phase III compilation) (ECI document, copy hosted by CEO Maharashtra)

rows.fact: BLAs could collect Form 6 claims and Form 7 objections from the public and file objections themselves with a prescribed declaration. Generic complaints without the prescribed form or declaration were not counted as claims or objections.
rows.quote: BLAs appointed by Political parties can collect Claims (Form 6) from public & Objection (Form 7) from public & file objection himself/herself along with prescribed declaration. Generic complaints, without prescribed Forms or declaration are not counted as Claims (Form 6) & Objections (Form 7).
rows.page_or_para: PIB release ID 2162605 (01 Sep 2025), footnote 1 to table A

rows.fact: An elector of the constituency could file a specific objection in Form 7. A person who was not an elector of that constituency could also object, with a declaration or oath under Rule 20(3)(b) of the 1960 Rules.
rows.quote: If any ineligible elector has got included: Any aggrieved elector of that Assembly Constituency can file specific Objection in Form 7 before 1 Sep 2025. ... Any person who is not an Elector of that Assembly Constituency can also file specific objection, along with declaration/oath as per Rule 20(3) (b)of the RER 1960.
rows.page_or_para: PIB release ID 2162605 (01 Sep 2025), closing bullets

rows.fact: The BLA declaration linked from the ECI bulletin says the information is based on proper verification of the roll part given to the BLA, signed with the BLA's name and party.

rows.fact: The Rule 20(3)(b) declaration linked from the ECI bulletin is an oath by a person who is not an elector of the constituency, naming the person, part and serial number, and acknowledging Section 31 of the RP Act and Section 227 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Samhita.
rows.quote: 4. I further declare that, although I am not an elector of the said constituency, I have personal knowledge relevant to this case and am making this statement voluntarily.

rows.fact: The Form 7 PDF on the Voters' Service Portal lets an applicant seek deletion of another person on five grounds, including not an Indian citizen, with a declaration under Section 31 of the RP Act 1950. It sets no limit on the number of objections.

rows.fact: 24,949 claims and objections in Forms 6, 7, 8 and 6A were filed against the draft between 16.12.2025 and 19.01.2026, and forms pending from before the draft were processed with them. From all these forms 12,166 electors were added and 3,812 deleted, apart from 35,780 found ineligible at hearings.

A total of 8,803 numbers of electors have been included, and a total of 1,924 numbers of electors have been deleted from the Draft Electoral Roll.

rows.page_or_para: CEO Mizoram press note No. H.11011/06/2026-CEO dated 07.09.2026, para 3

rows.fact: On the Commission's agreement the Court directed that the public notice say people left off the draft may submit claims with a copy of their Aadhaar card.
rows.quote: (vii) In the public notice, it shall also be expressly mentioned that the aggrieved persons may submit their claims along with a copy of their Aadhar Card.
rows.page_or_para: W.P.(C) 640/2025 order of 14.08.2025, para 3(vii), page 8

rows.fact: The Court directed twelve recognised parties to instruct their BLAs to help voters submit the requisite forms with any of the eleven documents or with Aadhaar.
rows.quote: the aforesaid twelve political parties, acting through their respective Presidents of the Bihar State, shall issue specific instructions to their Booth Level Agents (BLAs) to assist voters ... in submitting the requisite forms along with any of the eleven documents specified in the SIR Notification or with their Aadhaar Card.
rows.page_or_para: Judgment 2026 INSC 564 (27.05.2026), para 10.11, page 13 (the 22.08.2025 order itself was not located)

rows.fact: The Commission stated before the Court that claims, objections and corrections could be submitted after the 01.09.2025 deadline and would be considered until the last date of nominations.
rows.quote: the Commission took a categorical stand that claims, objections, and corrections could be submitted even after the deadline of 01.09.2025. It was stated that the process of consideration of claims and objections would continue until the last date of nominations, and that all inclusions and exclusions would be duly integrated in the final roll.
rows.page_or_para: Judgment 2026 INSC 564, para 10.12, pages 13-14 (the 01.09.2025 order itself was not located)

rows.fact: The Court directed the Commission to accept Aadhaar as proof of identity, not citizenship, as the 12th document for inclusion or exclusion in Bihar, while allowing its genuineness to be verified.
rows.quote: Accordingly, we direct the Election Commission of India and its authorities to accept Aadhar Card as a proof of identity for the purpose of inclusion or exclusion in the revised voter list of the State of Bihar. Aadhaar Card, for this purpose, shall be treated as the 12th document by the Authorities.

rows.fact: For people flagged for logical discrepancies, the Court allowed documents and objections to be submitted through an authorised representative, who can be a BLA, and directed ten more days for claims, documents or objections.
rows.quote: (ii) Persons likely to be affected are permitted to submit their documents/objections through their authorized representative. Such an authorised representative can even be a Booth Level Agent (BLA). ... 5. The Election Commission of India shall issue instructions for providing an additional 10 days' time from the date of displaying the lists in the Panchayat Bhawans/Block Offices to all persons who have not yet submitted their claims, documents, or objections to do so within the extended period.
rows.page_or_para: W.P.(C) 1089/2025 order of 19.01.2026, paras 4(ii) and 5, pages 3-4

rows.fact: The judgment records that new voters had to submit Form 6 with the Annexure D declaration, and holds that the Commission may set a documentation framework for an SIR that departs from Form 6 under the 1960 Rules if the departure has a rational nexus to its object.
rows.quote: f. Any new voter was required to submit Form 6 along with a Declaration Form in Annexure D of the Impugned Order. ... It is true that Form 6, as prescribed under the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, sets out a framework of documentation; however, the same is tailored to the process of revision contemplated under Section 21(2) of the RP Act and may not, in all situations, be capable of literal application to an exercise of the present nature. The Commission, therefore, retains a degree of residual authority to formulate an appropriate documentation framework suited to the exigencies of a Special Intensive Revision.
rows.page_or_para: Judgment 2026 INSC 564, para 45 item f (page 58) and para 152 (page 106)

rows.fact: In its directions the Court held that the documentation regime is not arbitrary or contrary to the statutory scheme. It does not name the Annexure D declaration in that holding.
rows.quote: e) The documentation regime prescribed by the Commission represents a considered exercise of its administrative discretion in furtherance of its Constitutional mandate. ... We are, therefore, unable to hold that the impugned documentation framework is arbitrary or violative of the statutory scheme.
rows.page_or_para: Judgment 2026 INSC 564, para 186(e), page 122; see also para 158 (page 109) on substituting documents in Form 6
